`chain.jsonl` is generated by `tools/generate_chain_fixtures.py` against mmx-node
`ca6438b37c08007106d58efe4a990f6ecb276649`. The oracle extracts Node::init_chain,
header/space/VDF verification, history lookup, block/transaction validation and
execution. Method qualifiers change to harness classes. Genesis replaces only
the transaction file reader with a trusted asset map, plus apply/commit/logging
with capture stubs. The original construction/checks and linked Block methods
produce expected blocks; native input/output accessors and wrapping/clamping
arithmetic produce expected settlement. Reference source and databases are not
modified.

16 genesis rows include original mainnet and testnet13 configuration and data.
They compare full lossless blocks, hashes/commitments, balances/supply, deployments
and contract read-cost indexes. Mutations cover wrong networks/content hashes,
timestamp casts and difficulty multiplication, hardfork-2 genesis serialization,
invalid/missing mainnet relay transactions, fee/input/output settlement with
successful/failed supplied results and native exemptions for bootstrap
transaction IDs/static cost. Mainnet's separate project relay determines the
project address but is not included/deployed. A synthetic executable names a
nonexistent constructor to prove genesis does not run it.

The final row contains three native verified extensions: heights 1 and 2, then a
competing height-2 block after restoring the native parent snapshot. All execute
a signed transaction that writes contract storage and transfers funds. Expected
balances include farmer/project rewards, fees and the ancestor-derived VDF payout.
Both hardforks activate at height 2. The k8 witness comes from `work.jsonl`; fixture
discovery samples network names until genesis and its next challenge both satisfy
that proof's Y window. Only discovery is customized: actual admission runs the
original native CPU space/VDF verifiers and copied Node verification methods.

Rust tests apply the same sequence through ChainState, reopen after commits,
reject missing work/tampering without publication, rewind every ledger/archive
index together, apply the alternate block and reset/reinitialize genesis. Samples
of a torn final chain frame must recover the preceding ledger and tip together.
The DB's smaller-frame tests separately cover every truncation position and
injected write failure, including preservation of pre-existing pending writes.

These fixtures implement a selected-chain store, not the native node's complete
fork tree, independent orphan archive, wallet/trade history indexes, mempool,
validator voting or finality service.
